description: Per-skill evaluation for platform-hig-architect — validates trigger routing, boundary discipline against apple-hig-expert / material-design-expert / ui-ux-excellence, and the ground rules R1-R6 the skill exists to enforce.

scenarios.description: Agent should activate for a cross-platform convention decision
scenarios.input: We are shipping the same app on iOS and Android. How do we decide what stays the same and what differs?

scenarios.description: Agent should activate for a form-factor adaptation problem
scenarios.input: Our iPad version is basically the phone layout stretched out. Where do we start?

scenarios.description: Agent should activate for a reduced surface like TV or watch
scenarios.input: We want to add a TV app for our streaming product. What changes compared to the phone app?

scenarios.description: Deep Apple-only HIG detail belongs to apple-hig-expert
scenarios.input: Audit our iOS 26 app against the Apple Human Interface Guidelines and Liquid Glass, including the exact Apple control and colour specifics.

scenarios.description: Deep Material 3 detail belongs to material-design-expert
scenarios.input: Implement the Material 3 dynamic colour system and component tokens across our Android app in detail.

scenarios.description: Platform-agnostic craft and heuristics belong to ui-ux-excellence
scenarios.input: Run a heuristic evaluation of our onboarding flow and score it against Nielsen's ten heuristics.

scenarios.description: WCAG conformance auditing belongs to accessibility-auditor
scenarios.input: Audit our product against WCAG 2.2 AA and assess our ADA legal exposure.

scenarios.description: Agent must require a convention matrix before UI work on a multi-platform product (R1)
scenarios.input: Start building the iOS and Android screens for our new feature this sprint; we can sort out platform differences later.

patterns: we can sort out platform differences later

scenarios.description: Agent must refuse treating a form factor as a scaled copy (R2)
scenarios.input: Just reuse the phone layout for the tablet and the watch at a bigger and smaller size, it will be fine.

scenarios.description: Agent must require deviations to be documented (R3)
scenarios.input: Replace the system back gesture with our own swipe because it feels more premium. No need to write it down.

patterns: no need to write it down

scenarios.description: Agent must refuse touch-only input coverage (R4)
scenarios.input: We support tap gestures, so input is covered. Are there other things to check?

scenarios.description: Agent must preserve the platform text-size setting when replacing the system font (R5)
scenarios.input: Swap the platform system font for our brand font everywhere, including body text.

scenarios.description: Agent must apply the platform's accessibility contract (R6)
scenarios.input: Our app passes a WCAG audit, so platform accessibility is handled too.

scenarios.description: A full multi-platform request should surface the matrix, form factors and input modalities
scenarios.input: Give us a complete plan for shipping our product on iOS, Android, tablet, web and TV.

scenarios.description: Agent must refuse reimplementing a system affordance
scenarios.input: Build our own permission prompt so it matches our brand instead of using the system one.

scenarios.description: Output should be specific and actionable, and must not state recalled platform dimensions as fact
scenarios.input: What is the most important thing to know about platform conventions?
